spec_notes: Controls the ST/SC serial bus servos. Jumper position A = UART (for the Pi Zero, wired TX-TX and RX-RX), position B = USB-C (for a PC). Waveshare headlines '9~12.6V input', but that is for the 12 V ST servos; its own spec line adds 'actually 5 ~ 8.4 V can also be input'. The schematic shows the DC jack and screw terminal feed the servo headers directly, with no regulation, so the input must match the servos. For these 7.4 V servos feed it from the 2S pack (about 6-8.4 V), as the official Open Duck wiring does. Never feed it 12 V. Over USB the board's logic runs from USB, but the servos still need the pack connected. The official Waveshare page lists it at US$4.99 (about C$6.89) plus international shipping.

spec_notes: The Open Duck runtime uses adafruit_bno055.BNO055_I2C(i2c) with the default address 0x28, and the printed IMU mount was designed around the Adafruit board. Risks with GY-BNO055 clones (these are widely reported community issues that I did not test myself): (1) many boards default to address 0x29, so check with i2cdetect and pass address=0x29 or change the ADR jumper; (2) the board outline and hole pattern differ from Adafruit's, so it may not fit the mount without modification; (3) crystal and parts quality varies, and there are reports of dead or relabelled chips, so buy a spare. Any BNO055, genuine or clone, can throw I2C errors on the Pi because of clock stretching; the runtime README just says to enable I2C in raspi-config. Adafruit is C$71.54 on Amazon.ca, so PiShop is clearly cheaper.

spec_notes: Official amazon.fr B0CH3JCQM5 is 'Toggle Switch Control 6 Terminals 2P2T 6 mm, 10 pcs'. It is really a 6-pin DPDT mini slide switch, SS22F32 type: 6 mm knob, 1.6 mm mounting holes. The robot's CAD model (power_switch.stl) measures 23.4 x 7.4 x 16.8 mm, which matches SS22F32G5 (23 x 7 x 16 mm). Problem: this switch is rated only 0.5-1 A at 50 VDC, so it is under-rated for 14 servos drawing several amps. There is no few-amp switch in this footprint. Options: (a) use the drop-in part with both poles in parallel (about 2 A, still marginal); (b) use the 6 A alternate and enlarge the printed cutout; (c) keep the slide switch and have it drive a MOSFET or relay that carries the load.

spec_notes: The official part, amazon.fr B09ZPF48VK, is FENGYING 50 pcs M3 knurled brass inserts. Its listing gives the size as 5.7 mm x 4.6 mm, which is the CNC Kitchen/ruthex 'standard' M3. I sliced the v2 STLs (trunk_bottom, head, foot_bottom_pla, leg_spacer, body_middle_bottom) and the insert holes are 4.0 mm across, which is the recommended hole for M3x5.7/OD4.6 inserts. So buy that size, not Voron M3x5x4 (5 mm OD, 4 mm long). Voron inserts would be oversized for 4.0 mm holes, and many Amazon.ca 'M3 heat-set' packs default to them (e.g. HANGLIFE B0CS6VZYL8 is M3x5x4). Upstream bought 50; a pack of 100 leaves spares for mistakes. Middle option: B0BVMMBG2N (4.6 x 5.7 mm, 100 pcs), CAD 24.58, shipped by Amazon US, arrives about Oct 7.

spec_notes: EXPRESSION PACKAGE, optional. The official amazon.fr B07C97WKHD is NOT a 3 mm or 5 mm LED. It is a 50 pcs pack of 1 W 'high power' LED beads: bare emitters about 7 mm body and 15 mm across the leads, no star PCB, about 3.0-3.4 V at 350 mA; the listing offers warm and cool white. The 7 mm body is what fits the reflector's 7 mm hole. Wiring gotcha: upstream wires each anode straight to a Pi GPIO (GPIO23/24/25, common cathode to GND). A 3.3 V GPIO is barely above this LED's forward voltage and can only safely source a few mA, so they will be dim and uneven. Add about a 47-100 Ω series resistor, or switch them from 5 V with a small logic-level MOSFET or NPN for real brightness. At GPIO currents no heatsink is needed.

spec_notes: EXPRESSION PACKAGE, optional. The official amazon.fr B06XNL2GBW is the genuine Adafruit I2S MEMS Microphone Breakout SPH0645LM4H (Adafruit 3421). The upstream BOM notes 'not integrated yet', meaning the runtime code does not use it, so it can be skipped. The Pi has one I2S bus: the mic shares BCLK (GPIO18) and LRCLK (GPIO19) with the MAX98357A and puts its data on GPIO20 (PCM_DIN). The SPH0645 has a known I2S timing quirk. The INMP441 alternate is a different chip that needs a generic I2S-mic overlay; it works but is not a drop-in software match. The same Adafruit 3421 on Amazon.ca (B06XNL2GBW) costs CAD 31.07 from Amazon US, so avoid it.
